entry.title: 'We Have To Know Why': Philanthropist Priscilla Chan’s Bold Bet On Rare Disease

media:group.media:title: 'We Have To Know Why': Philanthropist Priscilla Chan’s Bold Bet On Rare Disease
media:group.media:description:
In just a decade, rare disease groups have gone from not understanding certain genetic mutations to bringing gene therapies into clinical trials. Priscilla Chan joins Becky Quick to discuss rare disease research, personalized medicine and how AI could help advance biomedicine and science.
Chan and her husband, Mark Zuckerberg, the founder of Meta, co-founded the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) and Biohub, both with a core mission of curing, preventing, or managing all disease. Drawing on her background as a pediatrician, Chan explains how rare disease groups are building research programs, patient registries and clinical trials, and how this work could point to new approaches for treating diseases more broadly.
In this episode: 00:26 Introduction 03:02 Priscilla’s Road to Rare 13:07 Building the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative 20:20 Getting Back to Basics 30:30 Funding Rare Disease Pioneers

entry.title: Holiday deals: Can you trust AI to find them?

media:group.media:title: Holiday deals: Can you trust AI to find them?
media:group.media:description:
Artificial intelligence shopping tools can help consumers compare prices and find gift ideas, but experts say shoppers still need to verify unfamiliar retailers and sellers before buying. Scammers can use AI to make fake stores, product photos and reviews look convincing.
CNBC's Sharon Epperson has the latest on how to avoid AI scammers this holiday season.
